Twelve sprouts give about 150-170 ml of solid volume. Gaps between them bring the effective volume to about 130-150 ml.

**STEP 5 - Grams:** Whole cooked sprouts pack at about 0.8-1.0 g/ml, so 130-170 ml gives roughly 110-170 g. Counting individual sprouts at about 15-20 g each (cooked, slightly shrunken) gives about 180-220 g. I take a middle value of about 180 g.

**STEP 6 - Energy:** Cooked Brussels sprouts are about 35-45 kcal per 100 g. Roasted ones with some oil may be higher, so I use 45 kcal/100 g. 180 g × 0.45 ≈ 81 kcal.

**STEP 7 - Uncertainty:** Likely 180 g, plausible range 120-240 g. The energy range is about 55-110 kcal, depending on the weight and any hidden oil.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Twelve medium-small sprouts around 3 cm across should weigh roughly 150-220 g, so 180 g is plausible. Nothing visible suggests a large oil or sauce component, so I have not added any.

Total: about 180 g and about 80 kcal.
